speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry with regard to the latest G7 agreement on a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% (a) how will this potentially impact our efforts (including the use in part of corporate tax incentives) to attract MNCs; (b) what are the fiscal and foreign investment implications for Singapore; (c) which sectors of our economy will be principally affected; and (d) what strategies will the Ministry take to find new growth industries and hubs in this new global tax environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are closely monitoring developments and have been engaging industry stakeholders to understand their needs so that we can better formulate our response.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: After all, Singapore’s competitiveness goes beyond our taxation rates.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Key fundamentals such as our strategic location and international connectivity, excellent infrastructure, the rule of law and skilled workforce remain strong.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are, therefore, redoubling our efforts to enhance our competitiveness and improve our business environment, for example, through upgrading our Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are confident that investors will continue to find Singapore a compelling place to do business, and our economy can continue to thrive in the new environment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is a simple question: the impact of Pillar Two.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my first question is: will there be risk of these US firms moving out?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question is whether the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) is reviewing its strategies to attract multinational corporations (MNCs) in light of this change and what are those strategies?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think the Minister has mentioned briefly the non-tax factors but how much more can we improve to enhance even further those non-tax factors and to attract more firms coming in, year after year.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Yes, indeed, US firms play a very important role in Singapore's economy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They provide significant employment and good employment to Singaporean workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is not just the US firms.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think BEPS 2.0 is going to affect all countries and, therefore, it is important for us to take a holistic approach, look at the entire business environment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are doing quite a few things to ensure that we remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Mr Saktiandi asked whether there is a risk of firms moving out of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Companies will do their calculations and they do that almost yearly to decide whether they are going to continue to be in Singapore, to continue to invest more in Singapore or to move somewhere else.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why we cannot take it for granted, as I mentioned, and as the Finance Minister also underscored.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We need to continue to ensure that our business environment remains effective and competitive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: What are the things that MTI is looking at doing?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, we have to continue to invest in our infrastructure, to ensure that we provide a very efficient infrastructure to allow our companies to operate here in a very cost-effective way.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Over the last few weeks since I took on the job, I have been talking to our counterparts in other countries almost on a daily basis to develop new connections, to allow our companies to expand beyond the confines and the limitation of our physical size.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also want to encourage companies to invest in productivity and upgrading, so that they can continue to be cost-effective, and there are many schemes that we have offered.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I cannot detail all of them here; I am sure Members are aware there are a lot of support schemes to encourage and support companies to become more productive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Particularly, for tech companies, we have a lot of incentives and support for investment in research and development.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will anchor a knowledge-based economy, an innovation-driven economy, in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If we stop at where we are and hope that we will continue to thrive and to be vibrant, we will be in trouble.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have to constantly be on the move, look out for opportunities, continue to restructure, reorganise and reposition ourselves for new opportunities that will come our way.
